title: Six Weeks by the Bins
subtitle: 数据统计 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 数据统计（科学与技术·数据与统计）
meta: 主题语境：数据统计（科学与技术·数据与统计）　|　核心词汇：record　|　正文 337 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 record 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: Last term our statistics club decided to measure how much food our dining hall throws away. For six weeks we stood by the bins at lunch and ① recorded what went into them: rice, vegetables, whole pieces of bread. We also kept a written ② record of the weight, because memory is a poor instrument and neither of us trusted it.

The first week taught us very little, though we recorded everything carefully. The third week brought the hottest three days ③ on record for that month, and the amount of rice thrown away doubled. Our adviser suggested we ④ record our interviews with the cooks on my phone, so that we would not have to trust our notes alone. Listening back, I heard something I had missed: several students said the portions were simply too large.

Then the numbers turned embarrassing. In the week before the mid-term exams a ⑤ record four hundred plates went into the bins. We worked out the percentage of waste for each week and reached one conclusion. A popular explanation was that exam week makes people careless, but our data pointed to something duller: the larger trays.

Every school keeps a ⑥ record for each student, and ours now carries one line about this survey. My grandmother, who keeps her old vinyl ⑦ records on a shelf, laughed when I told her. She said every generation believes its own numbers are new. Then she said something I have quoted ever since, though she asked me to keep it ⑧ off the record: nobody ever weighed anything they truly loved.

By June we had enough evidence to speak to the head teacher. We ⑨ recorded the weekly figures in a single chart and asked for smaller trays; the school agreed to try them for a month. We ⑩ recorded a two-thirds drop in food waste before the summer holiday. Since then I record everything twice, once in the notebook and once on my phone. The difference was clear: six weeks, one chart, and a rule changed by two students with a scale.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 记录；记载（keep a record of）
C. adj./n. 创纪录的；最高纪录
G. 固定搭配：on record 有记载的；公开记录的
H. 固定搭配：off the record 非正式的；不得引用的

items.q: kept a written record of the weight
the hottest three days on record
record our interviews with the cooks on my phone
keeps a record for each student
her old vinyl records on a shelf
recorded the weekly figures in a single chart
recorded a two-thirds drop in food waste

answers.why: record＋宾语从句 what went into them，是动词“记录、登记”，与站在垃圾桶旁的动作相符。
a written record of the weight 是名词，keep a record of 意为“把……记录下来”，与手写称重相对应。
the hottest days on record 是固定说法，意为“有气象记录以来最热的日子”。
宾语是 interviews 且方式状语是 on my phone，说明是“录音”，下句 Listening back 也印证。
a record four hundred plates 意为“创纪录的四百个盘子”，record 作定语，表示数量达到最高。
学校为每名学生保存的材料，这里指学校档案，取名词“档案；记录”。
vinyl records 指黑胶唱片，与 kept on a shelf 搭配，是名词“唱片”。
off the record 意为“非正式的、不得公开引用的”，祖母让作者不要把这句话写进报告，而作者偏偏引用了。
record figures in a chart 是动词“把……记录／录入”，宾语为每周数据。
record a two-thirds drop 意为“记录到……下降了三分之二”，此处作动词，强调观察到的结果。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 六周里，我们记录下午餐时间被扔掉的一切。（record v.）
我们还把每天剩饭的重量记了下来。（keep a record of）
那是那个月有记载以来最热的三天。（on record）
我们用手机录了和厨师们的谈话。（record v.）
考试前那一周，创纪录地有四百个盘子被扔掉。（a record ...）
她让我不要把那句话写进报告。（off the record）
answers: For six weeks we recorded everything that was thrown away at lunch.
We also kept a record of the weight of the leftovers every day.
They were the hottest three days on record for that month.
We recorded our interviews with the cooks on my phone.
In the week before the exams, a record four hundred plates were thrown away.
She asked me to keep her words off the record.
